changes.summary: With invocation approval configured, the approver's instruction to merge authorizes delivery, including merges that deploy to production. Deploy adds drift approval, merge verification, and close-out. A direct chat instruction follows the configured merge policy without those steps.

Deploy verifies production when the workflow assigns it to the agent, checks the currently deployed revision, and leaves verification-dependent closures pending when the change is no longer deployed or the revision changes during checks.
Running Deploy again on a merged branch or naming the merged change request resumes ticket closure and production verification instead of stopping on an empty batch.
Deploy preserves newer work on a merged change request's remote branch and deletes eligible branches only when the remote tip still matches the original merged head.

Setup Snappedly Skills records what starts each agent step after a merge, proposes invocation approval where needed, and migrates the old stop-at-merge instruction to include close-out while preserving release actors and approval gates.

Deploy stops before any merge that would deploy to production without a recorded deployment approval gate or invocation approval. Rerun Setup Snappedly Skills after updating to configure the approval policy.

Clean Up leaves its edits unstaged and uncommitted on the current branch and shows what it changed, with check results and review findings. Committing happens on an explicit request or through Deploy.

Deploy commits the pending task changes first, including edits left by Clean Up, creates the task branch when you start on the base or default branch, and delivers the existing commit when nothing is pending.
Setup Snappedly Skills migrates existing workflow and agent instructions to the handoff from Clean Up to Deploy and preserves commit checks and delivery approval rules.
GitHub issue discovery fetches every page before filtering and counting triage queues. Setup Snappedly Skills refreshes the operation in existing repositories.
Deploy follows configured local, branch-only, and integration-branch delivery without requiring a hosted pull request.
Writing For Agents documents both Claude Code and Codex invocation settings and keeps them aligned.
Shared-reference guidance keeps distributed skill dependencies inside installed packages while allowing repository-owned context outside them.
The diagnostic reproduction script in Diagnosing Bugs prints the complete capture header and starts the first answer on its own line.

Snappedly Skills is publicly available under the MIT License: 26 engineering workflow skills for Claude Code, Codex, and other coding agents. Install every skill in one command, then type the setup command to configure your repository.

The main workflow takes a change from plan to merge. Grill settles the plan, Execute carries it out or works from an issue you name, Clean Up checks and commits the result, and Deploy opens the pull request and merges it once its checks pass.
Repository setup records your code host, work tracker, team workflow, domain docs, and frontend conventions, and every skill follows them.
Practice skills hold shared standards for code cleanup, code review, test-driven development, pull requests, and technical writing, and load when a task calls for them.
Upkeep and tool skills diagnose difficult bugs, survey a codebase's architecture, sweep out dead code, triage incoming issues and pull requests, resolve merge conflicts, and preview changes locally.
Triage reviews outside contributions without running their code on your machine. In a repository without workflow settings, Deploy stops before a merge that would deploy to production.
